newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden becoming low-inflation economy - Riksbank.
newsitem.headline: Sweden becoming low-inflation economy - Riksbank.

text.p: The governor of Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said on Thursday that confidence in Sweden's ability to keep inflation under control had increased internationally.
"What's happened...is that confidence in Sweden as a country of low inflation is now on its way to becoming established.
"This can be supported by continued firm fiscal policy and structural measures in the labour market...," Urban Backstrom said in a speech at a financial seminar.

Backstrom said the Riksbank's inflation target of two percent was well-balanced in light of recent studies describing the damaging effects of inflation and what can be regarded as "the optimal inflation rate."
He emphasised that it was just as important to avoid running under the target as over it.

On the subject of monetary policy, Backstrom repeated comments by the Riksbank on Wednesday that it would increase its intervention on the currency market to reduce volatility and stabilise the crown.
"We have a floating exchange rate in the full meaning of the term. It's the volatility we want to get at," Backstrom told reporters.

However Backstrom said the market should not read too much into the intervention. "I don't think you should over-dramatise our increased activity on the currency market. Most other central banks do it."
